title: The Next Wave of AI: Building, Scaling and Winning from the UK
description: AI has entered a new era: global platforms dominate, but fresh opportunities are emerging in infrastructure, ecosystems, and entirely new industries. Fresh off the launch of The Tech Nation Report 2026, our panel discusses the future of UK AI. Hear unfiltered stories from the front line on what it really takes to build, scale and compete from the UK today. Expect candid insights on product bets, platform dependence, talent and capital, and how founders are navigating the new AI infrastructure layer. Explore where the next wave of UK AI opportunity will come from, across high-growth sectors, emerging regions and founder-led breakthroughs.

title: Failure Isn’t Fatal but Playing It Safe Is
description: This session reframes failure as a critical engine for innovation and resilience. Founders share how they cultivate risk-taking cultures that turn setbacks into strategic fuel. - How can founders transform failure into momentum rather than fear? - Examine the habits that build courage, experimentation and resilience. - Distil the lessons that help companies move faster after getting it wrong.

title: From Volatility to Velocity
description: This fireside uncovers the strategy, pace and mindset behind the shift from hypergrowth to profitability. - How do you maintain clarity and resilience when the market moves against you? - Explore the strategic pivots that power profitable scale. - Understand what founders must prioritise during turbulent growth cycles.

title: Riding The Entrepreneurial Rodeo
description: Scaling brings intense highs, unexpected lows and rapid identity shifts for founders. This session explores how leaders evolve emotionally, develop resilience, and adapt as their companies outgrow them. - How does founder leadership need to evolve from early-stage creation to full scale? - Reflect on the emotional challenges that define the founder journey. - Explore the role of mentors, advisors and support systems at pivotal moments.

title: Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger.
description: Founders working at the edge of AI, health tech and advanced computation share how they build ambitious products while navigating competition, complexity and regulation. So, how are founders competing in a world moving faster than we can keep up with? - How are founders staying ahead as frontier technologies accelerate and competitors multiply? - Analyse what it takes to turn breakthrough ideas into defensible products. - Understand how to balance bold experimentation with disciplined execution.

title: The New Reality of Startup Value
description: As AI reshapes investment behaviour, founders must navigate a rapidly changing valuation landscape. This session highlights what realistic value creation looks like in 2026, the changes we’re seeing in the first half of the year, and how fast-growing companies are adapting. - What should founders expect from valuation trends in a post-hype AI market? - Analyse the widening gap between AI native companies and the rest. - Identify how funds are recalibrating their strategies and timelines.

title: In conversation with Alan Chang: How Fuse Energy Scaled in a Broken Market
description: Fuse Energy's growth story, how it's disrupting a broken sector, and why energy costs now matter more than ever.

title: Writing the Multi-Billion Dollar Playbook
description: Scaling from breakout success to planetary scale requires uncommon clarity, strategic boldness, and operational discipline. This session uncovers the real lessons behind building the world’s most ambitious tech companies. - How do founders identify and commit to bets with trillion-dollar potential? - Examine the uncomfortable truths behind scaling across continents. - Distil the patterns that separate category winners from fast followers.

title: Closing the Funding Gap for UK Scale
description: The UK AI sector is booming, yet founders still face structural gaps in scaling capital. This session explores where UK venture is heading, what needs to change and how founders can navigate the landscape effectively. - How will global VC shifts reshape UK founder opportunities in the coming years? - Examine why UK startups must build strong technical competencies earlier. - Understand how funds are adapting to founder requirements and new market demands.

title: In conversation with Alex Kendall: When Vision Meets Venture
description: Strong founder-investor partnerships are key to scaling with confidence. This session explores practical strategies for managing board dynamics, aligning expectations, and keeping vision on track while growing. - Examine how clarity and transparency shape effective board dynamics. - Identify the strategies that protect vision while navigating investor expectations. - Recognise when an investor isn’t the right fit and how to manage that exit.

title: Policy, Strategy, and Startups
description: A candid policy conversation exploring the direction of European innovation, regulation and global competitiveness. Founders gain insight into what they should expect from the next chapter of government strategy. - What policy direction will shape the UK’s tech landscape in 2026 and beyond? - Analyse how innovation, investment and regulation are being aligned nationally. - Explore the opportunities this creates for founders and scale ups.

title: Networking Break
From Manchester With Love: Supporting Innovation, Investment and Growth
description: Manchester didn't become the UK's fastest-growing tech sector by accident. It was built with intention. Over the past decade, Greater Manchester has developed a distinctive model for tech growth, one rooted in place, powered by devolution, and designed to last. This session brings together founders building transformational companies in Greater Manchester, including Manchester-born global data pioneer Matillion and ARM, which has chosen Manchester as its UK growth location, to explore what 'Manchesterism' really means in practice: a place-first philosophy that puts long-term, sustainable growth ahead of short-term noise. For founders and leaders at London Tech Week asking where to build something that genuinely changes the world, Manchester has spent a decade constructing an answer. The panel will unpack how devolved government has created the conditions that national policy often can't. From strategic planning and joined-up skills pipelines to genuine dialogue between industry and civic leadership. It will explore how a deliberate cluster model has produced world-class specialisation across AI and cybersecurity, and why diverse talent chooses to live, work and stay in the city region. This is a conversation about good growth: what it looks like, what makes it durable, and why the next generation of world-changing tech companies might just be built in Manchester.

title: The Untapped Talent Wave Powering Global Growth
description: Underrepresented founders face barriers that constrain their potential. This session examines what policy, capital and ecosystem action is needed to unlock full participation and economic impact. - What are the most significant obstacles facing underrepresented founders today? - Analyse how capital, networks and policy can unlock scale. - Identify the commitments required to build a more inclusive innovation economy.

title: Where Will The Next £100bn of Spinout Value Come From?
description: Universities and research centres are becoming powerful engines of innovation for the next generation of high growth companies. So what are the challenges and opportunities being faced, and how can ecosystems better support research-driven founders to disrupt the market and reach £bn potential? - How important are universities to the next wave of high growth innovation? - Identify the barriers preventing spinouts from scaling effectively.

title: Is The Value of Venture Capital Changing?
description: Founders’ expectations of venture capital are shifting fast. As market conditions evolve, the value-add founders look for from investors appears very different from just a few years ago. This session unpacks the new hierarchy of VC support, from the rising importance of capital access and customer introductions to the declining relevance of broader services. - Does access to capital take priority over access to customers? - Are traditional value-adds losing impact unless tied to fundraising or growth? - Understand why founders and VCs differ on board effectiveness and what meaningful governance looks like today.

title: Why Purpose Still Powers Performance
description: Purpose remains one of the most defining drivers of clarity, resilience and performance for founders and their teams. This session explores how a strong sense of why sustains culture and decision making at every stage of scale. - Learn how founders embed mission into culture to sustain high performance through scale. - What real-world tactics can entrepreneurs use to embed purpose into every process, ritual, and decision as they scale?

title: Maximising the UK's Talent Advantage
description: The UK is home to incredible talent, but we aren't fully maximising its potential. This session highlights how tech companies can make the most of Britain’s homegrown talent, while attracting the world’s best and brightest to the UK. It also explores the policies that would help rapidly scaling businesses find, hire, and retain the talent they need. - How to boost “talent velocity”, so companies can hire at a speed that matches their growth. - How to leverage existing government programmes and policies to bolster your talent pool. - Which new policies or measures would make the greatest difference for scaling businesses.

title: The Culture Tech Stack That Survives Hypergrowth
description: Culture evolves into organisational architecture as companies scale. This session explores how founders design systems, rituals, and structures that preserve identity and performance in fast-growing teams. - How can founders protect and scale culture from dozens to thousands of employees? - Identify the values, behaviours and processes that anchor strong organisations. - Examine how leaders embed clarity, cohesion and belonging across global teams.

title: The Rise of the Chief of Staff
description: As companies scale, founders need trusted partners to help translate vision into execution. This session looks at the all-encompassing role of the Chief of Staff, from strategic leverage and championing culture, to shaping leadership teams and how the role is becoming an indispensable position for founders. - How does the role enable founders to focus on high-impact priorities while ensuring execution across the organisation. - What are the skills, mindsets, and operational structures that make a Chief of Staff indispensable?

title: AI That Helps Humans Thrive
description: AI is transforming the workplace, but companies win when technology amplifies human capability rather than replacing it. This session explores skills, inclusion, and people-centred technological adoption. - How should leaders balance automation with human empowerment in the workplace? - Examine how ecosystems are accelerating AI literacy and opportunity. - Understand what skills teams will need to thrive in an AI driven economy.

title: Beyond the Exit: What Will Founders Be Remembered For?
description: Every founder’s journey is marked by milestones, the first hire, the first pivot, and eventually, the exit. But what remains once the day-to-day building is done? This panel explores the quiet shift from building a company to shaping a legacy. Join Marie, Marta, and Kathryn as they share how they’ve integrated a commitment to global impact into their entrepreneurial paths from the very beginning. Through the lens of the Founders Pledge community, we’ll discuss how a founder’s true work often begins where the exit ends, and how you can start defining what you’ll be remembered for today.

title: Networking Break
In Conversation with Max Junestrand | What It Really Took to Get Legora Off The Ground
New Jobs, New Roles, New Realities
description: AI is rewriting what work looks like, from the roles companies hire for to how organisations are structured. What new categories of work are emerging and what are the core competencies required for teams to thrive in an AI-shaped decade? - Which roles have emerged, are evolving, or are yet to be created? - How have structures, workflows, and leadership bandwidth shifted when humans and AI collaborate at scale? - What capabilities are required to stay competitive in an AI-accelerated economy?

title: Are We Human? Or Are We Augmented?
description: What does it mean to be human in an age of augmentation? Nearly a quarter of people report feeling lonely, raising urgent questions about the future of connection and wellbeing. This session explores how AI, relationships and culture are reshaping human experience. - How can society rebuild connection during a shift toward AI mediated relationships? - What are the psychological and cultural implications of AI companionship? - How can we stay ‘human’ in an increasingly automated world?

title: In conversation with Tom Hale: Oura's Next Chapter Navigating Growth in Wearable Tech
Building Europe’s Tech Sovereignty in the Era of AI and Quantum
description: Europe’s path to sovereignty now depends on scaling industrial capacity, securing critical supply chains and deploying frontier technologies at speed. This session defines what technological independence means in practice and explores how science, industry and policy must align to reduce strategic dependencies and strengthen resilience. What will it take to turn Europe’s scientific excellence into real sovereign capability? Explore how AI, quantum and advanced manufacturing form the foundations of Europe’s technology base. Learn how governments, innovators and investors are shifting from ambition to execution.

title: Tech Nation OnetoWin: Opening Remarks & Host Introduction
description: Opening remarks from Chantelle Young & Carolyn Dawson, followed by introduction to the Tech Nation OnetoWin host and judging panel.

title: Scaling Sovereign Innovation through Frontier Partnerships
description: Europe’s defence and industrial ambitions require faster adoption of deep tech, new procurement models and cross-border collaboration. This session explores how alliances between governments, investors and frontier founders are accelerating the journey from prototype to deployment. How can Europe scale dual-use technologies through faster, coordinated procurement? Examine how NIF, industry and startups are building shared adoption pathways. Learn how aligned demand and joint programmes can strengthen Europe’s industrial base.

title: Tech Nation OnetoWin: The Finalist Pitches
description: From cutting-edge AI to pioneering climate tech startups, each UK region is home to flourishing tech ecosystems with their own distinct strengths. 10 startups from across the UK will take to the stage in the hopes to secure an investment opportunity and showcase the vibrant regional innovation ecosystems that collectively strengthen the UK’s global edge. These are the next generation of tech leaders who will help define our digital economy for years to come.

title: Tech Nation OnetoWin: 2026 & Beyond: Technology Trends Shaping the Next Decade
description: A forward-looking investor-led discussion exploring the emerging technologies and market shifts that will define the next wave of UK startup success, from AI breakthroughs to climate innovation.

title: Tech Nation OnetoWin: Beyond London: Why the UK's Tech Future is Regional
description: Celebrating the powerhouse tech ecosystems across Manchester, Edinburgh, Bristol, and beyond, and why the UK's distributed innovation landscape is its greatest competitive advantage.

title: Tech Nation OnetoWin: The Final Showdown
description: The UK's most promising early-stage startups face live questioning from top-tier investor judges in a high-stakes pitch battle to crown Britain's next national champion.

title: Tech Nation OnetoWin: Winners Announcement
description: Celebrating the UK's newest national champion as we reveal which startup has won the competition, investment, and a global platform to scale their vision.

title: Speed-Running the Next Industrial Revolution: AI, Additive Manufacturing, and the Factories That Build Themselves
description: AI is transforming the entire engineering cycle, collapsing the time it takes to design, test, and manufacture physical products. What begins as a prompt will soon become a physical object, as AI reshapes the engineering input layer and next-generation additive manufacturing unlocks outputs that were previously impossible to build. How far can AI replace the traditional engineering stack, from CAD and simulation to materials and economics? What happens when AI starts designing things that only multi-material, multi-axis printing systems can produce? Could the UK lead the world in AI and advanced manufacturing and build the first truly adaptive industrial base?

title: Chairperson's Opening Remarks
Tech Nation's HealthTech Pitch Block
The LLM Will See You Now: How AI-First HealthTech is Redefining Patient Care
description: - Using AI to deliver more personalised, proactive and continuous patient care - Improving patient experiences through automation, clinical decision support and tailored treatment pathways - Addressing reliability, trust, privacy and regulatory challenges in AI-first health solutions

title: Regulatory Pathways 101 for HealthTech Founders
description: - FDA pathways, data governance, and practical strategies when building early - Understanding which regulatory pathways apply at pre-seed, seed and Series A - Avoiding common early mistakes that slow approvals or block market entry

title: Building Europe’s Deep Tech Backbone
description: Europe produces world-class deep tech, but too often it fails to scale because key technologies develop in isolation. AI, robotics, compute, energy and cyber are rarely designed to work together from the start. This session looks at what Europe still needs to build to fix that problem, from shared infrastructure and common standards to better ways of bringing founders, industry and institutions together. Focusing on what must exist before big partnerships and procurement can work, it explores how Europe can move from disconnected innovation to deep tech that scales. Why do Europe’s best technologies still struggle to scale together? How can ecosystems help technologies connect earlier? What will it take to turn strong local clusters into a joined-up European system?

title: Tech Nation's ClimateTech Pitch Block
The Rise of Dual-Use Innovation – A New Industrial Frontier
description: Dual-use innovation is reshaping Europe’s industrial landscape, with technologies built for defence increasingly driving commercial growth. This session uncovers how AI, autonomy, sensing and materials can scale across markets to strengthen both economic competitiveness and strategic capability. Could dual-use innovation become the engine of Europe’s next industrial era? Unpack how founders navigate procurement, regulation and investment to scale faster. See how dual-use technologies transform defence needs into commercial opportunity.

title: The Fifth Domain and the Future of Intelligent Infrastructure
description: As AI moves into physical systems and critical industry, control of the digital stack becomes a question of sovereignty, not just security. From trusted silicon and cryptographic hardware to AI reasoning systems and mission-critical deployment, Europe’s competitiveness now depends on who owns, secures and governs the full infrastructure layer. This session examines how secure compute, resilient AI architectures and operational cyber capability combine to form the sovereign foundation of Europe’s industrial future. Who really controls the sovereign AI stack, from hardware to decision systems to deployment? How do trusted silicon, cryptography and secure compute underpin AI safety and resilience? Where are Europe’s hidden dependencies in the infrastructure layer, and how do we reduce them? Can cyber resilience and AI assurance become drivers of growth rather than regulatory overhead?

title: How a New Generation of ClimateTech Founders Are Building Capital-Efficient, Fast-Moving Companies
description: - Implementing AI for climate modelling, optimisation, deployment and verification - Understanding the shift from infrastructure to software solutions

title: Founders of the Future Competition
description: - A flagship UK–US competition spotlighting the most impressive startups founded and led by under-25s on both sides of the Atlantic - Six finalists pitch live at London Tech Week, offering a rare chance to meet the next wave of transatlantic breakout founders before they hit the mainstream - One winner takes home a cash prize, with judges selecting the founder with the clearest path to global scale

title: Networking Break
Tech Nation's EdTech Pitch Block
The Transformation of Learning in the Digital Age
description: - How digital tools are reshaping the way people access, consume, and personalize learning - The role of AI, data, and platforms in creating more adaptive and engaging education - How educators and institutions can evolve to meet the needs of modern digital learners

title: Changing Lives Through Tech: Innovations to Prevent Homelessness
description: Hear from five entrepreneurs who will pitch their innovations that use data and tech to prevent homelessness See how philanthropic capital can help drive long-term, systems change Hosted in partnership with Venture Studio from Crisis and Homewards

title: The Upskilling Imperative: Preparing for the Jobs of Tomorrow
description: - What startups must prioritise now to stay competitive as roles shift faster than hiring pipelines can adapt - Innovating for economic growth

title: The Huntington’s Breakthrough: Challenging Genetic Fate Through Gene Therapy
description: A landmark medical milestone has occurred, slowing Huntington’s disease by 75%. Hear directly from the scientists behind this breakthrough and explore how gene therapy, neurosurgery, and real-time neural monitoring converged to make the impossible achievable. How did scientists slow the progression of Huntington’s disease for the first time in history? Discover how precision neurosurgery, viral gene delivery, and real-time data visualisation combined to create a world-first therapeutic success. See how this breakthrough could unlock new treatments — and eventually prevention — for a wide range of complex neurological conditions.

title: UK-Ukraine Investment Accelerator Pitches
description: The UK-Ukraine TechBridge 2026 edition returns to London Tech Week. Ukrainian tech has proven its resilience and innovation, and the capabilities on show have far-reaching potential. 10 Ukrainian startups will pitch their companies, offering investors and corporates early access to exceptional founders and the chance to partner with ambitious innovators bringing fresh technology and new ideas to the UK market. Come and meet the Ukrainian delegation.

title: Bridging Mind and Machine through Neurotechnology and Brain-Computer Interfaces
description: A UK patient with motor neurone disease controlled a computer using thought alone, only hours after receiving a Neuralink implant. This session explores how brain–computer interfaces are reshaping medicine, mobility, and human-machine connection. Could brain–computer interfaces restore independence for people living with paralysis? Hear how the UK’s first Neuralink trial, led by Professor Harith Akram and his team, is redefining what’s possible in neurotechnology. Explore how advances in implants, sensing, and neural engineering are moving BCIs from the lab into real-world clinical and assistive applications

title: Discovery that delivers: Turning Britain’s scientific edge into real-world impact
description: Join Kathleen Fisher, CEO of the Advanced Resarch Innovation Agency (ARIA) in conversation with Matt Clifford CBE, Chair of ARIA. Britain produces world-class science, but too often the path from breakthrough to real-world impact is slow, fragmented, or lost overseas. This session explores how the UK can turn its scientific edge into deployable technologies, scalable companies, and strategic advantage. From mission-driven funding to new models of venture creation, ARIA is rethinking how discovery translates into impact. Hear how the UK can move faster from lab to market, align science with national priorities, and build the industries that define the next decade. What does it take to turn world-leading science into real economic and strategic advantage for the UK? Where does the translation pipeline break down today, and how do we fix it at speed? How can mission-driven funding and new venture models accelerate the journey from discovery to deployment?

title: The Intelligent Lab and the Future of Discovery
description: AI-driven discovery is compressing scientific timelines from years to months. This session reveals how computational models, automated labs, and machine learning are transforming R&D across medicine, materials, and biology. Could intelligent systems make scientific discovery as fast and iterative as software innovation? Unpack how data, automation, and predictive modelling are accelerating molecular design, drug discovery, and biological engineering. See how the convergence of computation and biology is creating a new era of high-speed, high-precision scientific breakthroughs.

title: The Machine Layer of Medicine
description: Healthcare is entering a new structural phase. Intelligent machines are no longer confined to diagnostics or administration. They are becoming an operational layer within clinical systems. From surgeon-controlled robotics to automated logistics networks and microrobotic platforms operating inside living tissue, physical AI is reshaping how care is delivered, coordinated and executed. This session explores how the machine layer is being designed into modern healthcare, where it creates measurable value, and how leaders are defining the boundary between augmentation and delegation in high-stakes medical environments. How is the machine layer being integrated into core clinical systems without compromising safety or trust? Where does intelligent automation deliver real operational advantage, and where does it introduce new systemic risk? What responsibilities must remain permanently human as physical AI becomes embedded in care delivery?

title: The Science of De-Extinction
description: Join the founder of the world’s first de-extinction company, using breakthroughs in gene editing, conservation genomics and computational biology to revive lost species and engineer new tools for planetary-scale biodiversity and ecosystem restoration.

title: Greenprint for Growth: Scaling Farm Innovation to Protect Food Security
description: Did you know British farms are using drones in the fight against climate change – helping them spot from the air where irrigation or fertiliser might be needed? How do we move from piloting promising agri-tech innovations like this to scaling their mass adoption to safeguard Britain’s food security? As geopolitical events and climate shocks continue to disrupt global food supply chains, innovation and emerging tech will be crucial in ensuring we can continue to find ways to deliver a reliable supply of fresh, quality food. British agriculture is at the forefront of this transformation, pioneering new practices, processes and technology that will help protect the shopping basket in the years to come. Support for the sector to expand and ramp up this innovation has the power to not only secure our supply chain, but power growth and productivity, too. The session will bring together Tesco and a Tesco supplier. Drawing on their experiences of working together on Tesco’s first ever Low Carbon Concept Farm, they will explore what it takes to deliver agri-innovation at farm level and how collaboration across the value chain can accelerate progress.

title: Isambard AI and the Race to Tackle Humanity’s Biggest Challenges
description: The UK’s new Isambard AI supercomputer is powering breakthroughs across science, from decoding disease to modelling the planet and accelerating clean industry. How will exponential computing change the way we solve humanity’s biggest problems — and who gets access to its power? See how the UK’s most advanced supercomputer is enabling discoveries in climate science, medicine, and materials engineering that were once out of reach. Unpack what national AI infrastructure means for scientific leadership, industrial innovation, and the pace of global competitiveness.

title: Financing the Next Industrial Age: How Europe Funds Deep Tech at Scale
description: Europe’s deep-tech ambitions now hinge less on scientific discovery and more on whether its financial system can support scale. As frontier manufacturing, bio, energy and AI companies move from breakthrough to deployment, the question is no longer whether Europe can innovate, but whether it can finance industrial growth at speed, at home. This session examines the capital structures, public-private mechanisms and sovereign strategies required to turn European deep tech into globally competitive industrial leaders. What would it take to build a financial system capable of scaling Europe’s deep tech champions? Where do growth capital, pension funds, blended finance and corporate venture work well today, and where do they break down? What must Europe change now to ensure its most advanced companies can scale at home rather than being pushed to the US?

title: Intelligent Matter and the Materials of Tomorrow
description: AI is transforming how we discover and design the materials that will power human progress, accelerating breakthroughs across energy, electronics, and sustainable manufacturing. What if we could design the perfect material before it ever existed? Uncover how computational modelling and machine learning are cutting discovery cycles from years to months, unlocking a new era of materials innovation. See how intelligent design is creating the breakthrough materials that will power cleaner energy, smarter devices, and low-carbon industries.

title: The Limits of AI Data Centres and What Comes Next
description: AI’s rapid growth is pushing today’s data centre model toward hard limits in power, cooling and infrastructure. This session explores why those constraints are becoming unavoidable, which solutions can realistically extend Earth-based compute, and when more radical approaches may be required. The panel examines what must change to support AI at scale in the years ahead. Why are AI data centres hitting hard limits in power, cooling and grid capacity? Which solutions can realistically extend Earth-based compute and where do they fall short? When do off-world and alternative compute models begin to make strategic and economic sense?

title: Rebuilding the Mineral Value Chain: From Discovery to Sovereign Processing
description: Critical minerals underpin AI infrastructure, electrification and advanced manufacturing, yet Europe remains structurally exposed across discovery, extraction and refining. Geological scarcity is not the only constraint. The real bottlenecks sit in data, processing capacity, capital deployment and geopolitical concentration. This session explores how the mineral value chain is being redesigned end to end. From AI-driven subsurface intelligence and biological extraction methods to sovereign refining capacity, it examines how technology and industrial strategy can work together to build resilient, lower-impact and strategically secure supply systems for the decades ahead. Where are the real mineral bottlenecks, and are they geological, technological or geopolitical? How can AI-driven discovery and biological extraction materially reduce environmental impact while accelerating supply? What would it take for Europe to build sovereign refining capacity and secure the full mineral value chain?

title: Tech Nation Panel: No Shortcuts: Fundraising & Scaling as a Deeptech Founder
description: Hear from Tech Nation's deeptech scaleup founders across a range of verticals on the tough decisions that hurt short-term but ultimately made their companies survivable Raising before the tech was "ready" - what actually convinced investors to back deep technical risk without over-promising? What breaks first when you start to scale: people, process, or product? Mistakes you wouldn't repeat - and the ones you would

title: Why Enterprises Need to Think about Geospatial AI, Today
description: Leaders across agriculture, insurance, energy, forestry, supply chain, and beyond are turning to Geospatial AI to understand their changing environments. How a living, daily map of Earth imagery when fused with advanced AI analysis - called Planetary Intelligence - unlocks unprecedented insights to drive corporate decision-making. How automated change-detection algorithms are transforming corporate strategy, enabling enterprise leaders to automate asset monitoring, mitigate risk and respond to crises in real time.

title: Preparing for Space: The Making of an Astronaut
The Space Infrastructure Race
description: Space is now critical infrastructure. Satellites underpin AI, finance, climate systems and defence. As orbital assets multiply and geopolitical tension rises, sovereignty in space becomes an industrial question, not a symbolic one. This session examines how nations build, deploy and protect dual-use space capability at scale, turning commercial innovation into interoperable, resilient systems across trusted partners. What space capabilities must allied nations physically build, secure and coordinate to remain strategically resilient in the 2030s? How do dual-use space systems move from venture-backed startups to trusted infrastructure? Where do orbital, launch, data or supply chain dependencies quietly undermine collective security at scale?

title: Steering the Future of the Space Economy
description: Space is now critical national infrastructure, underpinning connectivity, navigation and timing, climate and environmental monitoring, and national security. This fireside will explore how the UK is translating the National Space Strategy and Space Industrial Plan into delivery: strengthening priority sovereign capabilities including satellite communications, Earth observation, launch and space domain awareness, building a more competitive UK space economy, and ensuring the UK remains a leader in safe, sustainable and well-regulated space activity. It will also examine how the government is improving the “golden thread” from strategy to policy to execution to accelerate delivery and unlock private investment. What are the two or three UK space capabilities the government is prioritising this decade, and what must change to deliver them faster? How will the UK turn space policy into industrial growth, exports and private investment while keeping critical capabilities anchored in the UK? How can the UK balance rapid commercial growth with leadership on space sustainability, safety and long-term resilience of the services the economy depends on?

title: How to Solve the Space Debris Problem
description: Earth’s orbit is becoming crowded, chaotic and fragile. Tens of thousands of defunct satellites and fragments now threaten the infrastructure we depend on for navigation, communication and climate monitoring. As commercial launches accelerate, the question is no longer if we should act, but how fast we can. Can innovation outpace the chaos of congestion in space? Explore the new wave of startups, agencies and alliances developing debris-removal, tracking and avoidance technologies. Reveal how the race to protect orbit is reshaping regulation, insurance and the long-term future of space commerce.

title: When The Lights Go Out On The ISS…
description: As the International Space Station nears the end of its operational life, a new race is underway to design the platforms that will replace it. Private companies, space agencies, and new international alliances are redefining what orbital infrastructure looks like. The future is more modular, more commercial, and built for science, manufacturing, and maybe even tourism. What will succeed the ISS, and who will own and operate the next generation of orbital stations? Explore how commercial space platforms are shifting from government-led experiments to thriving industrial ecosystems in orbit. Reveal how these new stations could unlock advances in research, manufacturing, and human habitation that reshape life on and beyond Earth.

title: The Age of the New Space Entrepreneur
description: A new wave of founders is commercialising space, turning exploration into enterprise. From launch systems and satellite networks to in-orbit research and biomanufacturing, these entrepreneurs are building the infrastructure and industries that will define the next space economy. Who are the founders turning the space frontier into viable, scalable markets across science, industry and infrastructure? Explore how venture capital, public funding and sovereign initiatives are fuelling the rise of NewSpace companies across the UK and Europe. Discover how the business of space is shifting from exploration to commercial platforms and industrial capability, unlocking opportunities spanning materials, communications, energy and microgravity-enabled research.

title: How General-Purpose Robotics Is Rewiring Industry
description: Robotics is moving beyond single-task automation toward intelligent physical systems that can adapt across tasks, environments and workflows. Enabled by advances in embodied AI, perception and system-level orchestration, general-purpose robotics is turning robots into flexible industrial agents, reshaping productivity, resilience and the nature of work across manufacturing, logistics and infrastructure. What separates general-purpose robotics from traditional automation, and where is true physical intelligence emerging today? How do layered robotics systems enable scalable deployment across complex, real-world environments? Why are integration, workforce design and human-robot collaboration now the critical barriers to adoption?

title: Reigniting the Spirit of Innovation
description: What happened to our appetite for risk? Once the driving force of progress, the courage to fail has given way to a culture of caution. In this conversation with the founder of Gravity Industries, we explore how bold ideas, persistence and experimentation can restore the inventive spirit that fuels prosperity and progress. Why has our collective appetite for failure, the true engine of discovery, faded? Explore how entrepreneurship can restore ambition, resilience and creative confidence in a risk-averse world. Uncover what it really takes to build breakthrough ideas when the greatest risk is not daring at all.

title: When Supply Chains Start to Think
description: Physical AI is moving from the lab to the warehouse, the port and the production line. Robots and autonomous systems are beginning to sense, decide and act in real time, reshaping how goods move through the global economy. As disruption, geopolitics and climate pressures expose vulnerabilities, the next wave of intelligent automation could redefine resilience itself. How will physical AI transform the way we make, move and manage products? Explore how robotics, sensors and predictive systems are building more agile, transparent and self-healing supply chains. Reveal how autonomy at every layer of logistics can strengthen economic resilience and competitiveness.

title: Chairperson's Opening Remarks
Tech Nation's Intelligence 2.0 Pitch Block
Permission to Innovate: What It Really Means to Build a Company With AI at the Core
description: - AI-first startups driving growth in 2026

title: The Proximity Advantage: Building from and for the Edges
description: The most resilient innovations don't come from building for the average user. They come from building for the edges, and what happens when everyone benefits. Apart from lived experience, various other essential ingredients in the ecosystem must adapt and coordinate to enable innovation from the edges, including reframing this with social impact and how other such players come into the mix. This session brings together perspectives to make an urgent argument to the startup and investor community: proximity to a problem is a competitive advantage, and the ecosystem is systematically undervaluing the founders and organisations who have it most.

title: Grow London Global
Reshaping the Legal Landscape with AI
Opening Remarks: Why the UK, Why Now?
description: Discover why the UK is a leading destination for founders and top international talent Explore the latest trends shaping careers, entrepreneurship, and innovation in the UK.

title: London Tech Week Opening Keynote Address
Shaping the Future of Work and Opportunity in the UK
description: Exploring how AI can drive productivity, fuel economic growth, and position the UK as a global AI leader. Demonstrating how “Frontier Firms” are using AI to transform how work gets done and what it takes for other organisations across the nation to follow. Discussing why closing the skills gap and expanding access to digital careers is essential for unlocking talent and delivering shared prosperity.

title: Leading the UK Into the Next Wave of AI: From Adoption to Transformation
description: Why breadth of AI adoption alone isn't enough — and what it takes to go deeper From employee productivity to agentic systems: how the most advanced organisations are rewriting what's possible The five leadership tensions that will define who captures value in the next wave

title: AI is the Computer.
description: Examining how AI is evolving computing both technically and philosophically, as operating systems advance from taking instructions to taking objectives. Illustrating how value in AI is shifting from individual model families to systems that can orchestrate work across tools, models, tasks, and environments. Addressing how this shift will redefine the platforms people use every day and shape the future of work.

title: The Emerging Case for Sovereign AI Development in Europe
description: Is it now a must for Europe to focus on sovereign AI development to safeguard our economies, uphold core values, and ultimately remain competitive? Can Europe's commitment to ethical development, environmental sustainability, and AI's broader societal purpose be reflected in AI developed elsewhere? Discussing the implications of the growing reliance on US hyperscalers or Chinese tech giants and strategies to mitigate the potential risks.

title: The Future of Human-Technology Interaction
description: Exploring why audio is poised to surpass text as the primary interface between user and technology and how AI is driving this transformation. Detailing how this groundbreaking shift is elevating the potential of AI agents, creating smarter, more adaptable and universally accessible support for businesses. Assessing how to build user trust and demonstrate the tangible value of audio-first technology to prepare populations for a dramatic shift in the way we use technology.

title: Mind the Agentic AI Gap: From Boardroom Optimism to Workforce Readiness
description: Discussing how to bridge the gap between executive ambition and workforce experience, where *86% of leaders plan increase AI investment, but only *20% of employees feel involved in shaping its impact. Exploring why reinventing the work, workforce, and workbench is required to realise the value of agentic AI in the UK through new roles, new capabilities, modular architectures, and trust frameworks. Analysing how new upskilling methods like **co-learning—a dynamic process where people and AI learn together in the flow of work—are essential to achieving workforce readiness. * Pulse of Change, 15 January 2026 | ** Learning, Reinvented: Accelerating human–AI collaboration

title: Empowering the 99% in the Age of the Builder
description: Exploring how AI-powered vibe coding is democratising access to software development, enabling anyone with an idea to create new apps and products. Sharing how Lovable is already bringing value to the enterprise, radically reshaping the boundaries of workplace creativity and innovation. Discussing whether vibe coding could redefine how new businesses are built, potentially enabling the rise of a unicorn company built by a single employee.

title: Investing in AI: Trends, Challenges, and the Road Ahead
description: Debating which characteristics make AI companies most appealing to top VCs and how scaling companies should position themselves for their next funding round. Which industries will dominate future funding rounds? Are there currently underappreciated sectors with untapped opportunity for AI investment? Spotlighting the most promising emerging AI companies worldwide and examining how these organisations are positioned to transform industries and reshape enterprise operations.

title: Networking Break
Chairperson Opening Remarks
Powering the World's AI Ambitions
description: With the success of AI companies hinging on the scale and quality of supporting infrastructure, what measures are being taken to meet these critical demands? Beyond data centres, what other infrastructure investments are essential for a country to become an AI superpower? Are current infrastructure initiatives sufficient for the long term, or are we relying too heavily on the assumption that AI will soon become less energy-intensive?

title: How AI and Digital Finance Will Power the Next Financial System
description: Outlining the steps required for agent-driven financial services, starting with the reconstruction of legacy financial infrastructure to suit machines as well as people. Exploring how to create secure, regulated digital wallets for agents to safely and responsibly hold and transfer value, manage digital assets, and execute transactions. Explaining the emerging trend of wallet-based rather than account-based finance and its critical role in shaping the next-generation financial system.

title: Securing the Future of AI: The Roadmap to Safe & Ethical AI
description: What is being prioritised to ensure that increasingly complex AI models that can drive, carry out surgical work, and design consumer products are safe and reliable? Exploring the growing momentum behind explainability and reasoning implementation alongside established governance councils, frameworks and model cards. Why innovation thrives within guardrails; hear real-life examples of how work on governance has been conducive to innovation rather than a barrier.

title: Why Open Source is Key to AI’s Next Chapter
description: Exploring why the next generation of AI companies are embracing open source for lower costs, reduced structural AI bias and enhanced innovation through shared learning and collaboration. Debating whether a rejection of proprietary AI in favour of a more collaborative approach to development will accelerate progress towards the next wave of AI breakthroughs. Discussing why an open-source approach is critical for the input of startups, academics, and underrepresented communities, ensuring AI serves society as a whole.

title: Chairperson's Opening Remarks
AI for Global Impact: Solving the Defining Challenges of Our Time
description: Does AI hold the key to overcoming challenges, like finding cures to deadly disease and reversing climate change effects, that have so far eluded even our greatest minds? What is the ceiling of AI as a transformative force for societal advancement and how do we unlock this potential? How can governments, venture capital, and other stakeholders encourage the emergence and scaling of more mission-led AI companies?

title: An AI-Driven Approach to Safeguarding a Nation
description: Examining how responsibly deployed, AI‑enhanced data processing supports the timely, evidence‑based decision‑making needed to maintain intelligence and security advantage while retaining human judgement and oversight. Exploring how responsibly designed and tested threat‑detection technologies can identify and prioritise critical security risks in real time, with a focus on accuracy, transparency, and operational assurance. Providing insight into how cyberthreats are evolving, what the most advanced emerging attacks are today, and government’s guidance on defending against them.

title: From UK Innovation to Global Roads: How Wayve's Embodied AI Is Shaping the Future of Autonomous Vehicles
description: Uncovering how a British AI company is leveraging real world data and a unique end-to-end learning approach to create road-ready, scalable driving intelligence for global markets. Diving into the extensive safety practices that are enhancing reliability and fostering public trust in an emerging technology. Discussing what’s required to move from early pilots to everyday autonomous mobility and what this progress means for the UK's leadership in the future of transport.

title: Chairperson's Closing Remarks
How AI is Transforming Drug Discovery
description: Analysing how predictive and generative AI models are revealing new treatments, predicting treatment success, and expediting the time to market for life-saving medicine. Exploring how AI is amplifying the impact of leading scientific minds by modelling biological systems and providing unprecedented insight into the function of the human body. What can other industries learn from the use of AI for drug discovery? Exploring how the technology behind ground-breaking processes can be replicated within other fields.

title: From Supply Chain Chaos to Control
description: Supply chains are the backbone of modern business, but inefficiencies and disruptions can create chaos that ripples across operations and destroys customer satisfaction. This session delves into how organisations can harness the power of AI to transform supply chain management, turning unpredictability into precision. How can organisations leverage AI to optimise supply chain operations and reduce inefficiencies? Exploring the role of predictive analytics and machine learning in improving demand forecasting, inventory management, and logistics. Real-world examples of AI-driven supply chain transformations that have enhanced operational resilience and customer satisfaction. Discussing the challenges of implementing AI in complex supply chains and strategies to overcome them.

title: Will Quantum be the Driving Force Behind the Next Wave of AI Breakthroughs?
description: How will the promise of quantum computing to drastically increase computational power and efficiency amplify AI’s impact on industry and wider society? When will quantum computing converge with AI at scale, and which sectors are poised to benefit most from this transformative intersection? Examining the most significant technological advancements in quantum computing over the past year and their potential to reshape enterprise AI strategy.

title: Digital Twins as the New Crystal Ball
description: In an era of increasing complexity, digital twins are emerging as a game-changing tool for supply chain management. By creating virtual replicas of physical processes, organisations can simulate, monitor, and optimise operations in real time. How are digital twins revolutionising supply chain management across industries? Exploring how to effectively deploy the tech to enable real-time simulation, monitoring, and optimisation of supply chain processes. Discussing the integration of AI with digital twins to predict disruptions, customer behaviours, improve efficiency, and ultimately enhance decision-making.

title: What World-Leading AI-Powered Customer Experience Looks Like
description: Uncovering how are the most innovative B2C brands are delivering experiences that satisfy even the most AI-savvy customers with sky-high expectations. Exploring how advances in machine learning and deep learning are unlocking deeper customer understanding enabling greater personalisation. In a world of endless AI-powered CX possibilities, how are major brands focusing on meaningful features that drive loyalty and sales, rather than falling for AI gimmicks?

title: Redefining Customer Engagement with AI-Enhanced Portals
description: Customer engagement is evolving, and AI-powered portals are at the forefront of this transformation. These intelligent platforms are reshaping how organisations interact with their customers, offering personalised, seamless, and efficient experiences. How are AI-powered customer portals transforming the way organisations interact with their customers? Discussing the integration of chatbots, virtual assistants, and predictive analytics into customer portals for enhanced functionality. Real-world examples of organisations that have successfully implemented AI-powered portals and analysing how that has impacted customer behaviours.

title: Reimagining Creativity and Experiences in Modern Entertainment
description: Discussing how creative teams are leveraging AI to revolutionize content creation and presentation and attain strategies for how this can be employed within traditional enterprise. What do modern audiences demand from entertainment providers and how will AI help deliver on these demands? What can audiences expect from entertainment 5 years from now once the industry has been able to fully comprehend where AI can bring real value to audiences?

description: What does it take to create value with AI and move beyond experimentation? Where is AI making an impact across our value chain? How are we leveraging insights to develop tools to optimise customer interactions? How HEINEKEN leverages AI to improve customer interaction?

description: Payments are a pivotal moment in the customer journey, where operational efficiency meets customer satisfaction. This session explores how organisations can optimise payment processes to enhance the overall customer experience, reduce friction, and build loyalty. How can organisations leverage AI and automation to create seamless, secure, and efficient payment experiences for customers? Exploring the role of customer data and AI in offering tailored payment methods, such as instalments, subscriptions, or one-click payments, to meet diverse customer needs. Real-world examples of organisations that have transformed their payment processes to improve customer loyalty and operational resilience.

title: The Human-AI Dance
description: As AI becomes more integrated into customer interactions, the challenge lies in balancing automation with the human touch. This session explores how organisations can blend the strengths of AI, such as efficiency and personalisation, with the empathy and nuance of human expertise. How can organisations strike the perfect balance between automation and the human touch in customer interactions? Exploring the role of AI in enhancing empathy, personalisation, and seamless customer journeys. Discussing when to let AI take the lead and when human intervention is essential for meaningful engagement. Real-world examples of companies blending AI and human expertise to deliver exceptional customer experiences.

title: How Agentic Systems are Rewriting the Banking Playbook
description: Exploring how AI is advancing faster than enterprises can absorb, with pilots and agents often lacking the governance, context, and operational control needed for secure production in regulated environments like Banking and Financial Services. Examining the challenges created by fragmented architectures, vendor lock-in, and inconsistent governance as enterprises try to scale agentic systems across mission-critical workflows. Introducing the OutSystems Agentic Systems Platform, a unified, open operating system for building, orchestrating, and governing AI across mission-critical agents, apps, and workflows.

title: How Agentic AI is Transforming Financial Services
description: As artificial intelligence evolves, its ability to act autonomously and make decisions is reshaping financial services. This session explores how agentic AI is driving innovation, improving efficiency, and enabling smarter decision-making across the industry. How is agentic AI automating complex processes and enhancing operational efficiency within the world’s biggest financial organisations? Exploring the role of AI in delivering real-time insights and predictive analytics for better financial outcomes. Examining how technology leaders are determining the best use cases to deploy agentic solutions and how they’re measuring the ROI.

title: From Algorithms to Autonomous Delivery: Bringing Innovative AI Tech to Small Business
description: Discussing Miki's journey, from co-founding Wolt to joining forces with DoorDash and becoming the CEO of Deliveroo in October last year. Unpacking how the company is using AI and tech as an equaliser for local businesses, helping high street restaurants and shops grow and compete with e-commerce giants. Exploring how Deliveroo, DoorDash, and Wolt are piloting drones and robots across their different markets to serve local businesses and consumers.

title: Unlocking the Power of Data for Smarter Financial Decisions
description: In today’s fast-paced corporate environment, data is more than just numbers, it’s the foundation for smarter, faster, and more strategic financial decisions. This session dives into how finance professionals can unlock the full potential of AI to drive innovation and gain a competitive advantage. How can finance professionals harness AI and advanced analytics to make more informed, data-driven decisions? Exploring more advanced use cases to get more from data. Discussing the importance of data governance, quality, and security in ensuring reliable decision-making. Success stories of organisations that have transformed their decision-making processes through data-driven strategies.

title: How are Enterprises Preparing for Agentic Commerce & AI-Assisted Purchasing?
description: As more customers gravitate towards LLM’s rather than traditional search engines for online shopping, how are enterprises adapting to ensure they capitalise on this trend? How should enterprises be rethinking the design of their websites and customer journeys to accommodate AI agents, not humans, as the primary online browsers? Assessing how far we are from fully agentic commerce and how enterprises can help facilitate seamless purchasing in an AI-driven marketplace.

title: The Path to a Fully Autonomous AI-Bank
description: We’re starting to see the term ‘AI-Bank’ being thrown around across retail, corporate and institutional services. While many challenger banks and traditional names are adopting AI for an increasing number of functions, the vision of a fully ‘AI-Bank’ still feels far away for many. But what would it mean for clients and customers, employees, and the future of financial services as we know it? What are the biggest technological and organisational challenges in building a fully autonomous AI-Bank, and how can they be overcome? How can an AI-Bank balance automation with transparency, trust, and ethical decision-making to ensure customer confidence? What will the rise of AI-Banks mean for the workforce, and how can financial institutions prepare employees for this transformation?

title: Driving Innovation Toward a Greener Future
description: Examining how AI-powered solutions are accelerating efforts to combat climate change and achieve global sustainability goals, including net-zero emissions by 2050. What major challenges must be overcome to successfully scale transformative AI-driven technologies for environmental impact? How is AI enabling precise modelling and predictive analytics to identify the most effective strategies for sustainable development across industries?

title: Driving Innovation in Regulated Industries
description: Innovating within highly regulated industries like financial services is challenging but not impossible. This session examines how leaders are navigating strict regulations to develop transformative AI solutions, leveraging sensitive data responsibly while staying agile in a rapidly evolving landscape. Exploring the processes and safeguards being deployed to minimise risks while leveraging highly sensitive information. Discussing the most effective strategies for enterprises to seize emerging opportunities and mitigate future risks in regulated environments. Success stories of game-changing AI deployed within the financial services sector.

title: Is Advanced Automation the Answer to Public Sector Revitalisation?
description: How can public sector organisations, renowned for their legacy systems and slower adoption of new technologies, ensure they are not left behind in the AI revolution? Dissecting plans to turbocharge Robotic Process Automation, Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing and further streamline labour-intensive public sector processes. What can the public expect in terms of public service transformation driven by AI?

title: Chairperson's Closing Remarks
AI-Driven Fraud Prevention in Action
description: Considering the growing threat of bad actors looking to defraud customers, empowering financial organisations to detect and respond to threats with unprecedented speed and precision has never been as important. This session delves into the transformative role of AI in safeguarding financial systems. How is AI improving the accuracy and efficiency of fraud prevention in financial services? Exploring the use of advance machine learning models, specifically anomaly detection and predictive models, to identify suspicious activities. Addressing the most common hurdles in deploying AI-driven fraud prevention systems and strategies to overcome them.

title: Chairperson's Opening Remarks
Navigating the Evolving Payments Landscape with Emerging Technologies
description: Emerging payment technologies like blockchain, cryptocurrencies, and digital innovations are transforming the payments landscape, creating new opportunities and challenges for financial service leaders. This panel explores how organisations can adapt and thrive in this dynamic ecosystem. How are advancements in AI, blockchain, and other technologies shaping the future of payments? Exploring the rise of cryptocurrencies, contactless payments, and digital wallets in transforming payment systems. Discussing the challenges and opportunities that this new landscape presents to financial service leaders. Insights into how organisations can stay ahead in the rapidly evolving payments ecosystem.

title: Assessing the Business Impact of Responsible Innovation
description: Discover how enterprises are using responsible AI underpinned by robust data governance, risk assessment, and security practices to drive progress towards key business objectives. What demonstrable impact has responsible AI development had on customer relationships and the willingness of staff to adopt new tools and ways of working? Hear how robust data governance, strict model design guidelines, and advanced explainability has ensured AI tools that deliver secure and reliable outcomes.

title: Ensuring Compliance in the Age of AI
description: As AI becomes integral to financial services, ensuring compliance with complex regulations is more critical than ever. This session examines how AI can streamline compliance processes while maintaining transparency, ethics, and accountability. How can finance professionals leverage AI to navigate complex regulatory requirements and ensure compliance? Exploring the role of AI in automating compliance processes, monitoring transactions, and identifying potential risks. Discussing the importance of transparency, explainability, and ethical considerations in AI-driven compliance systems. Real-world examples of financial service organisations that have successfully implemented AI to enhance compliance and reduce regulatory risks.

title: Networking Break
How Tech & AI is Streamlining Previously Complex Processes and Accelerating Growth
description: Uncovering how GSK is integrating data, tech and AI at pace across the enterprise to simplify how people work and free up teams to focus on science, patients and growth. Highlighting how GSK has redesigned workflows to empower employees to leverage AI more effectively, enabling faster decisions, sharper execution, and smarter resource allocation. Delving into AI’s starring role in driving faster medicine and vaccine delivery by streamlining discovery, development, and regulatory processes.

title: Transforming Financial Planning with AI-Driven Insights
description: Technology is transforming corporate finance by enabling more precise forecasting, smarter decision-making, and optimised resource allocation. This panel explores how organisations can harness this to enhance financial planning and analysis (FP&A) for strategic growth. How is AI revolutionising financial planning and analysis to enable more accurate forecasting and budgeting? Exploring the role of machine learning and predictive analytics in identifying trends, improving decision-making, and optimising resource allocation. Real-world examples of organisations leveraging AI to enhance FP&A processes and drive strategic growth, exploring their successes and the challenges they faced in integrating the technology into existing legacy environments.

title: The Workplace in 2031: What Will AI-First Organisations Look Like 5 Years from Now?
description: Presenting a 5-year roadmap for organisations aiming to become AI-first, highlighting key challenges that must be addressed today to secure future success. Exploring AI’s expected effect on traditional enterprise workflows and organisational structures and why adapting now will be critical to thriving in an AI-driven future.

title: Redefining the CFO Role in 2026
description: The role of the CFO is undergoing a profound transformation, shifting from traditional financial oversight to driving innovation and strategic growth. This session explores how CFOs can adapt to meet the demands of a dynamic business landscape. How is the role of the CFO evolving from financial steward to strategic business leader? Exploring how CFOs can leverage technology and data to drive innovation, improve operational efficiency, and create value. Discussing the importance of cross-functional collaboration and how CFOs can lead digital transformation initiatives. Insights into how CFOs can balance short-term financial goals with long-term strategic vision in a rapidly changing business environment.

title: Optimising Liquidity with Advanced Technologies
description: Liquidity management is changing as advanced technologies are enabling organisations to maintain greater financial stability and operational efficiency. This panel explores how businesses can leverage these tools to optimise liquidity strategies. How are AI and automation transforming liquidity management to ensure financial stability and operational efficiency? Exploring the role of predictive analytics in cash flow forecasting and liquidity planning. Discussing the integration of real-time data and AI-driven tools to enhance visibility and control over liquidity.

Exploring how to seamlessly deploy agents that quietly eliminate friction, enhance productivity, and deliver rapid ROI without adding operational complexity. Discussing why prioritising measurable outcomes and continuous performance optimisation is essential for enhancing reliability and unlocking greater long-term value.

This session explores how finance leaders can collaborate with CEOs and technology to rebuild resilience, align teams, and lead organisations through complex transformations. How can finance take the lead in stabilising operations and setting the stage for long-term growth? Exploring strategies for fostering collaboration between boards, executives, and teams to ensure a unified direction. Discussing Practical approaches to maintaining focus and progress when change is slow and challenging.

title: Leveraging AI to Strengthen Enterprise Cyber Resilience
description: Several recent high-profile data leaks have exposed the extent of the cyberthreat to modern enterprises. Will AI prove it is the solution to turn the tide on the rising threats? How can enterprises quickly adapt to defend against emerging threats like AI-generated deepfakes and increasingly sophisticated social engineering attacks? Building on the early promise shown by AI tools for threat detection and identification of vulnerabilities, what other tools should now be a priority for enterprise?

description: With the rise of text to image and text to video Gen AI tools, the path from idea to execution can be incredibly fast. Yet this accessibility has brought the rise of what’s being called ‘AI Slop’, so how are the best in the business approaching this rapidly changing? How can marketing leaders ensure generative AI is used effectively to deliver high-quality, impactful campaigns? Exploring strategies to avoid inefficiencies and misaligned outputs when scaling generative AI for content creation and customer engagement. Which tools work best and how have creative teams integrated them effectively into their creative workflows? Discussing best practices for training generative AI models to align with brand voice, messaging, and business goals.

Is brand consistency still critical in an era where personalisation dominates marketing strategies? Discussing the ethical considerations and governance frameworks required to ensure responsible use of agentic AI in marketing.

description: As the digital marketing landscape shifts towards a privacy-first future, the disappearance of third-party cookies presents both challenges and opportunities. With third-party cookies disappearing, what alternative strategies can sales and marketing leaders adopt to maintain effective targeting and personalisation? How can AI-powered tools and first-party data help brands build stronger, more direct relationships with their audiences? description: Standing out as a brand requires more than just visibility, it demands cultural resonance. Identifying strategies to ensure AI models are continuously updated with real-time, business-critical insights for sustained relevance and accuracy.

How Hexagon simplified its narrative, visual identity, and digital ecosystem to scale at AI speed How to translate advanced technology into human relevance – and why this matters more than ever Exploring the role AI played in accelerating consistency, speed, and content governance without losing brand integrity and the key lessons for marketing leaders embarking on their own transformations in complex, matrixed, global organisations

Turning Trends into Impactful Narratives
description: In an era where cultural conversations are shaped by digital platforms like Pinterest, TikTok and Instagram, marketers must master the art of identifying and leveraging trends to craft stories that captivate audiences. This session explores how to harness real-time data and insights to create narratives that resonate deeply and drive meaningful engagement. How can marketers monitor and analyse trends across platforms like TikTok to uncover cultural moments and shape timely, relevant campaigns? How can advanced analytics tools be used to personalise storytelling at scale, ensuring narratives align with individual customer behaviours and preferences? Exploring the role of machine learning in trend detection, audience segmentation, and the creation of predictive, data-driven narratives that align with evolving marketing strategies.

title: Unlocking Value from Customer Loyalty by Turning Fans into Advocates
description: Turning loyal customers and fans into passionate promoters, leveraging their authentic recommendations (word-of-mouth, reviews, UGC) to build trust, awareness, and drive sales is one of the most effective marketing methods. But how can you drive greater advocacy for your business? Discussing how to effectively find your most engaged and satisfied customers and help them succeed with your product to earn their loyalty. Exploring the options of how we can offer spaces for them to share their positive experiences. Debating the best ways to motivate and reward advocacy and encourage further support.

title: A Look Under the Hood of an Award-Winning Marketing Team
description: We’ve explored the essential pillars of transformation across people, processes, and technology needed to elevate your sales and marketing strategy. But what happens when these elements seamlessly come together? Imagine best-in-class marketers empowered by cutting-edge technology. This session dives into a compelling case study of a team that has led from the front, revolutionising their organisation’s performance through outstanding sales and marketing innovation.

title: What is Quantum and Why it Matters Now
description: Quantum computing is rapidly moving from theory to reality, capturing global attention as breakthroughs accelerate. This session cuts through the complexity to reveal what quantum is, why it matters now, and how it’s fast becoming a defining force in science, security, and innovation. Unpacking quantum computing’s core principles and its unique ability to solve problems classical computing cannot address. Why quantum is rapidly rising up national and global agendas as countries race to lead the next wave of technological change. Exploring where we are on the quantum timeline — what’s real today, what’s still emerging, and how fast the next decade could accelerate

title: Breakthroughs, Bottlenecks, and What Remains Impossible
description: Quantum is entering a pivotal phase where extraordinary scientific progress meets some of the toughest engineering challenges in modern technology. This session explores the breakthroughs driving the field forward, the limits still holding it back, and the critical milestones the world must reach to unlock quantum’s full potential. How are recent advances in hardware architectures, algorithms, and system performance reshaping quantum's technical landscape? What barriers still constrain scalability and reliability, from qubit stability to error correction? What fundamental technical milestones must be achieved before quantum advantage becomes widespread?

title: Leveraging Quantum Technologies for the Enterprise Today
description: Enterprises are beginning to see real gains from quantum computing as early projects deliver faster optimisation, sharper risk insights, and more efficient operations. This session highlights how organisations are already putting quantum to work, where it is proving most effective, and the industries starting to feel the impact. How are the leading quantum computing companies delivering value to enterprises today? Exploring real‑world use cases where the technology has been deployed for optimisation, risk analysis, and supply chain management. Discussing the industries that are currently benefiting most from quantum computing solutions.

title: Building Tomorrow's Society with Quantum
description: Quantum technologies are beginning to reshape how public services plan, model, and respond to national challenges. This session brings together public‑sector teams to share real‑world applications and explore how quantum could transform decision‑making, public services, and national capabilities in the years ahead. Where are public‑sector‑led quantum applications already demonstrating maturity beyond enterprise adoption? How could quantum computing transform climate modelling, mobility systems, emergency response, and long‑term infrastructure planning? How are public‑sector environments approaching quantum experimentation and strategic investment? What broader societal benefits could emerge from quantum‑enabled public services?

title: Industry Frontiers in Quantum
description: Industry’s early adopters are now putting quantum to work on high‑value commercial challenges. Organisations across finance, pharma, and complex industrial systems are testing quantum for modelling, discovery, and optimisation. This session explores how these early moves are beginning to reshape innovation and competitiveness. Discussing how financial institutions are advancing modelling, scenario analysis, and portfolio optimisation with quantum methods Exploring how pharma and biotech are accelerating molecular simulation and drug discovery through quantum‑enabled approaches Unpacking how complex industrial systems are applying quantum to optimise engineering, production, and large‑scale operational processes

title: The Innovation Pipeline: Universities and Spinouts Driving Quantum's Future
description: Universities are delivering the breakthroughs and nurturing the talent that will shape the next era of quantum. This session explores how academic discoveries progress into commercial ventures, what it takes to accelerate research‑to‑innovation pathways, and how the UK can strengthen its position by attracting and supporting world‑class researchers. How are universities driving foundational quantum research and breakthrough innovation? What pathways exist from academic discovery to commercial spinout, and what factors enable successful progression from lab to market? How can we accelerate technology transfer, support early‑stage quantum ventures, and build a thriving innovation pipeline? How can the UK, as a global quantum leader, attract, support, and retain international research talent within its innovation ecosystem?

title: National Initiatives and International Collaboration
description: National quantum programmes are accelerating worldwide, creating new opportunities for deeper collaboration and shared capability. This session looks at how the UK can strengthen partnerships with key allies, build on emerging frameworks and scale its own national initiatives to stay competitive in a rapidly evolving global landscape. With China investing billions into their quantum efforts, when viewing this as a technological race, many are suggesting that the UK, Europe, and U.S. must collaborate to prevail, but what’s being done and how can the UK do more? How can we build upon the UK-U.S. Tech partnership announced as part of the recent State Visit? What initiatives/programmes are there within the UK to foster innovation and development of quantum technologies?

Hear from international founders who chose the UK to build and scale, and discover the companies shaping the next chapter of UK innovation.
