description: Lightning presentation from ecosystem advisors sharing quick-fire advice for startups accessing the UK market.

title: UK GTM: How to scale and succeed in the UK market
description: Expanding to the UK is a transformative milestone, but can require a fundamental shift in strategy to ensure success. This session brings together a powerhouse panel of immigrant founders, growth experts, and investors to share the raw, real-world realities of the UK Go-To-Market journey. From navigating the UK’s regulatory landscapes to hiring your first in-region leaders, our experts will deconstruct what it actually takes to win in the British ecosystem.

title: Chairperson's Opening Remarks
Supercharging AI Development with Smarter Cloud Strategies
description: Exploring how enterprises can design cloud environments for AI that can support diverse applications, manage complex data, and facilitate scale. Evaluating the role of containerisation, Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS), and other next-generation tools in accelerating AI development within the cloud. What measures must be taken to ensure seamless access to diverse, secure, and real time data essential for AI accuracy and effectiveness?

title: Rethinking SaaS for the AI-Driven Enterprise
description: Examining how enterprises are redefining contracts and expectations with traditional cloud providers and MSPs to align with new AI-driven operational goals. Debating which elements of traditional SaaS services can be carried out more effectively by AI agents, saving costs, increasing enterprise agility and enabling greater customisation. Analysing how the market is most likely to adapt and what enterprises can expect from the next generation of SaaS providers operating in the AI era.

title: Containing the Spiralling Costs of Growth
description: Discussing how to enhance the effectiveness of FinOps teams charged with recapturing wasted cloud spend and ensuring cloud investments are aligned with business goals. Examining strategies for controlling the costs of managed service providers without affecting the quality of cloud operations. Uncovering key strategies to achieve significant cost savings through supplier diversification and reduced dependency on a small number of vendors.

title: Securing the Cloud: Best Practices for 2026 and Beyond
description: Uncovering how enterprises are adapting to curtail the heightened data security risk of increasing workload migration to the cloud. What are the most effective strategies for tackling common threats to cloud security like misconfigurations and insecure interfaces? Exploring how businesses are implementing AI-powered threat detection, autonomous monitoring, and response capabilities for more robust defences.

title: Building Flexible and Scalable Architectures to Boost Enterprise Agility
description: Debating how enterprises can achieve the cloud flexibility required to adapt to evolving client needs, shifting strategic priorities, or changes to internal resources. Examining the steps tech leaders are taking to advance multi-cloud strategies that empower enterprises to innovate with greater autonomy. Exploring how approaches such as containerisation and composable architecture can enhance the ability to operate more efficiently across multiple providers.

title: Private, Public or On-Prem; Managing Workloads Across Different Environments
description: Turn workload placement into a strategic advantage; balance cost, performance, latency, and compliance with smarter decision-making across environments. Master hybrid and multi-cloud complexity; build portability and avoid vendor lock-in while keeping flexibility at scale. Gain full control with unified visibility; leverage observability and centralised management to run workloads seamlessly anywhere.

title: Driving Business Innovation with Real Time Data at the Edge
description: How is edge computing helping contemporary businesses deliver the services customers want most much faster and cost-effectively than ever before? Exploring how increasing volumes of available real time data is impacting the success of businesses across a variety of industries. Evaluating what types of data should be processed and stored at the edge as opposed to in the cloud. What is the right balance that enterprises should strive to strike?

title: Networking Break
Defining the Cyber ‘Must-Haves’ for Enterprises in 2026
description: Identifying the core cybersecurity measures enterprises must adopt to safeguard their data in the face of a dramatic surge in the number of cyberattacks in recent years. Examining how enterprise security strategies and tools are evolving to counter more potent threats like AI-enabled social engineering and deepfakes. Dissecting how enterprises can overcome severe resource constraints to deploy the complex, multi-layered security frameworks required today’s threat landscape.

title: Chairperson's Opening Remarks
Installing Impenetrable IoT & Remote Device Security
description: Exploring advanced initiatives beyond secure-by-design principles to enhance IoT and remote device security. Discussing how tech leaders are ensuring embedded software is secure to prevent the need for real-time patching. Projecting what the future risks opened up by IoT, and remote device use will be and how tech execs can defend against these risks.

title: Ensuring Growing AI Use Isn’t Increasing Security Risk
description: Highlighting key strategies for securing internal AI tools, including controlling access and preventing the use of sensitive information in prompts. Examining best practices for auditing and monitoring internal AI usage to identify and mitigate unforeseen risks and potentially harmful user behaviour. Analysing how enterprise are the addressing security risks posed by increasing numbers of staff experimenting with unsanctioned AI tools.

title: Creating a Cyber-Savvy Workforce to Combat Modern Threats
description: Outlining how can enterprises ensure that employees remain informed about emerging risks and effective countermeasures as the threat landscape evolves rapidly. How can enterprises equip staff to recognise and respond to increasingly sophisticated AI-enabled social engineering attacks? What innovative new tools are available to empower staff to repel emerging cyber risks easily and effectively?

title: Shielding Your Business from Third-Party Risk
description: Outlining key measures enterprises should be taking to fortify increasingly complex and high-risk supply chains containing numerous third-party vendors. How can technology leaders enhance visibility of interactions with each individual supplier to more accurately assess security risk? What new partner screening practices should every organisation be adopting to minimise the risk of introducing new vulnerabilities into their security framework?

title: Building Enterprise Resilience for the Quantum Era
description: Examining the validity of security concerns surrounding the deployment of quantum computing at scale, including the heightened vulnerability of existing encryption methods. How can governments, regulators, and vendors better educate enterprises on emerging risks as quantum technology continues to evolve? Outlining actionable steps for enterprise tech leaders to safeguard digital assets against the security challenges posed by quantum integration.

Chairperson's Opening Remarks

Debating the relative importance of data architecture in creating a data-driven organisation, versus fostering a data-centric culture, interoperability, or streamlined access to insights. How has the recent rise of data lakehouses altered the way that large enterprises are approaching data storage, management, and analysis?

title: From Data Overload to AI-Driven Excellence
description: Creating a clear roadmap for collecting and unifying critical enterprise data from diverse sources, enabling the development of high-impact AI tools. How are enterprises contextualising different data sets to ensure accurate interpretation and relevant insights that align with organisational goals? Exploring how Centrica is contextualising different data sets to ensure the governance and compliance of data used for AI systems.

title: Designing Enterprise Data Strategies to Thrive in the AI Era
description: What strategies are large companies using to reduce energy consumption to sustainable levels as AI usage continues to expand? How are enterprises collaborating with third party AI and data partners to improve data energy efficiency? Evaluating the practicality of individual enterprises building their own data centres to meet rising energy demands and support AI-driven operations.

description: As workforces evolve and roles become more complex, organisations are looking for new ways to ensure critical knowledge is maintained and consistently accessible. National Grid and Capgemini will showcase how an AI‑powered digital mentor is capturing the lived experience of expert engineers and making that knowledge available on demand to apprentices and early‑career professionals. The session will explore how enterprise‑grade GPTs can support faster learning, safer decision‑making and more resilient workforce capability

title: Transforming Customer Data into Deeper Relationships
description: What new methods are being used to transform raw customer information into actionable data that positively transforms customer offerings and experiences? How are behavioural, demographic, and transactional data being leveraged to deepen the connection between customers and their favourite and most essential services? Assessing the most valuable types of customer data and whether companies with a holistic view of the customer retain a competitive advantage in 2026.

title: Driving Data Excellence with Smarter, Faster, and More Resilient Networks
description: Uncovering how enterprises are boosting the speed and reliability of crowded networks to unlock improved access to data and drive major workforce efficiency gains. Analysing the critical role of AI in enhancing bandwidth allocation, reducing data latency, and creating uninterrupted access to real-time insights for data-driven decision-making. Evaluating the impact of continuous network monitoring on issue detection, minimum connectivity speeds, and enabling data-intensive applications like AI and analytics.

title: Assessing Synthetic Data’s Impact on Organisational Insight, AI Reliability and Enterprise Security
description: Examining how enterprises are leveraging synthetic data to enhance customer and operational insight when traditional data collection is limited or restricted. How can tech leaders ensure the use of synthetic data in AI system development is a net-positive, boosting AI reliability rather than hindering it? Exploring how synthetic data is minimising risk and strengthening enterprise security by reducing reliance on sensitive data during system or product development.

description: Examining how recent advances in AI, data platforms, and edge computing are accelerating the adoption and value of digital twins across different environments including built, natural, and social. Exploring the impact of a growing range of digital twins use cases, from city‑scale planning, asset performance optimisation, and infrastructure operations to safety, resilience, and emissions reduction. Discussing why a broader range of industries are increasingly using digital twins as a core decision‑making tool - moving beyond pilots to embed data-driven insights across the full lifecycle of systems, products, and operational environments.

description: Exploring how tech leaders are harnessing data to empower disparate workforces to successfully execute high impact, complex projects with global scope. Uncovering how to navigate differing regional regulations and preferred tech partners to provide all employees worldwide with equal access to critical data and tools. What initiatives are tech leaders installing to install universal interoperability across the various systems used across the organisation?

description: Breaking down how LBG’s approach has challenged legacy processes typical of large corporate entities to achieve a more agile delivery. Their approach to creating consistency in API standards and making those standards stick with targeted training and use of AI.

Examining what it takes to build a truly customer-first AI agent able to earn the trust and loyalty of users disillusioned by the failures of traditional customer service chatbots. How is Sierra designing AI agents that integrate effortlessly into the operations of the world’s biggest brands?

description: Europe is rebuilding the defence and industrial capabilities required for an era shaped by autonomy, AI and intensifying geopolitical competition. Sovereignty now depends on scaling industrial capacity, accelerating innovation cycles and aligning policy with deployment at speed. This session explores how Europe strengthens its industrial base, accelerates adoption of advanced systems and reduces critical dependencies. From software-defined defence to modernised manufacturing and cross-border procurement, it examines how a sovereign defence era is being built in practice. Where is Europe already moving at speed, and where must it go further? How are AI, autonomy and software-led systems reshaping capability development? What must governments, industry and investors now execute to unlock a modern, sovereign industrial base?

title: Building Secure AI Agents You Can Rely On
description: Exploring strategies for verifying, authorising, and tracing all deployed AI agents, reducing the security risks posed by unidentifiable ‘ghost agents’ Discussing how to establish clear boundaries for agent activity to prevent rogue behaviours like erroneous contract generation and accessing unauthorised data sets. Developing a blueprint for rigorous agent testing to ensure they respond correctly to security threats and avoid opening up vulnerabilities for attackers to exploit

title: Averting Disaster Through Robust Recovery Frameworks
description: 74% of the UK’s largest enterprises experienced a data breach in 2025*. With breaches becoming near inevitable, how can recovery plans sufficiently minimise operational disruption and preserve client trust? Exploring advanced strategies for implementing emergency protocols, encouraging effective staff response and ensuring critical systems remain functional during disturbance. Examining how measures such as decentralised data storage can reduce vulnerabilities and prevent single points of failure during breaches or disasters. * UK Cyber Security Breaches Survey 2025 produced by the UK Government Department for Science, Innovation and Technology.

title: The Role of AI in Driving Sustainable Mobility
description: Spotlighting AI’s pivotal role in advancing battery design and optimising energy management. Showcasing how cloud-based language models are enhancing user experience through NEV-specific innovations including intelligent car cabins and next generation voice interactions. Exploring solutions to overcome the final barriers to widespread electric-vehicle adoption, such as offering recharging as fast as refuelling.

title: How Vinted is Making Second-hand the First Choice Worldwide
description: From a small start-up in Vilnius to Europe’s leading second-hand platform, Vinted has changed how people buy and sell second-hand. In this session, Adam Jay (CEO, Vinted Marketplace) sits down with Avantika Chilkoti (The Economist) to explain how Vinted Marketplace has grown across 26 markets, and beyond fashion to all kinds of household items. Learn how the company makes second-hand easy, reliable, and affordable, and what’s next as it builds the infrastructure for a global second-hand economy.

Powering Context-Aware AI: How AMD is Enabling Trusted, High-Performance Enterprise Intelligence
description: Discussing why next-generation AI models must understand the context of their working environment and the needs of the employees they serve to unlock another level of value for enterprises. Assessing how enterprises can implement AI systems that are adaptable and continuously evolve by learning from changes in organisational operations and employee behaviours. Highlighting how context-awareness training also reduces AI bias and strengthens trust in models through more specific and consistently reliable results.

description: The global AI market has entered a new phase of consolidation, with players like OpenAI reshaping business models, redirecting capital flows, and redefining competition. The Tech Nation Report 2026 unpacks these shifts, focusing on where the UK can win, which sectors are set to grow, and how founders are adapting in a rapidly evolving landscape. Get the headline findings from The Tech Nation Report 2026, the definitive state of the nation report on UK tech since 2015. Discover where the next wave of UK AI growth is coming from, including the sectors, regions and technologies moving fastest. Discover what founders want from policymakers to unlock UK AI growth.

Highlighting the importance of open, mission-driven collaboration between government, industry, and academia to establish AI infrastructure that delivers lasting economic and societal benefits.

Managers of Infinite Minds: Knowledge Work in the AI Age
description: Framing AI as a ‘miracle material’ for the modern age - like steel and semiconductors before it - that will transform the speed and shape of knowledge work, both at an individual and organisational level. Discussing why collaborative AI - intuitive tools built on shared context, workflows, and governance - is the key to unlocking AI’s potential for companies of all sizes. Exploring how, as capability becomes increasingly commoditised through AI, differentiation moves to human judgement, taste, and agency. Sharing what Notion as a company is hiring for and building towards with that lens.

Presentation by Kipp Bodnar, Chief Marketing Officer, HubSpot
AI Has an Infrastructure Problem
description: Everyone is talking about AI models but far fewer are talking about what actually makes them work. This session challenges the idea that AI success is about software alone, shifting the focus to the networks, latency and security that power it in the real world. As AI moves into live environments, UK organisations are rethinking what matters: control, resilience, and accountability. We’ll explore why trusted telecom infrastructure is becoming critical to deploying AI at scale. What comes next: how VodafoneThree’s £11bn investment is building the infrastructure AI depends on strengthening the UK’s connectivity, security, and compute foundations for the decade ahead.

title: Ukraine’s Innovation Blueprint for a Resilient Future
description: Ukraine has built a powerful innovation ecosystem under the pressure of war — fast, adaptive, mission-driven, and deeply connected to real-world needs. The next challenge is to ensure that this technological potential is not lost as the country moves from survival to recovery, but becomes a foundation for long-term transformation. While much of the world discusses dual-use technologies as the adaptation of civilian innovation for defense, Ukraine now faces the reverse task: translating defense-born technologies into peaceful applications. This session will explore how Ukraine can preserve, scale and responsibly adapt the technological breakthroughs developed in wartime and what this experience reveals about the role of innovation in addressing the challenges facing societies globally. From rebuilding critical infrastructure and strengthening public safety to improving crisis response and democratic security, Ukraine offers a practical case study of how technology can move from urgent necessity to long-term public value.

title: The Comprehension Gap: How to Trust AI Agents with Expert Knowledge
description: Why the agentic enterprise will be decided at the knowledge layer — and what the 2% of organisations successfully crossing from pilot to production have figured out. How governing and verifying enterprise knowledge bottom-up unlocks accuracy rates that cross the threshold from interesting to deployable, with real examples from manufacturing, telecoms, and industrial engineering. What it takes to make expert knowledge scalable and traceable — and the $150Bn Market opportunity awaiting players like Iris.ai who are solving it.

title: Fireside Chat with Salesforce
AI is Smart. Humans are Genius: why the future of talent is not what you think.
description: For decades, hiring has rewarded people who know the right answers and execute reliably. But AI is changing the value of human work. As execution becomes faster, cheaper, and more abundant, the skills that once defined top talent are being rewritten. Knowledge, compliance, and execution are no longer enough. The next advantage will come from the deeply human capabilities AI cannot easily replicate: judgment, imagination, empathy, taste, curiosity, and the ability to frame better questions, weigh trade-offs, and make better decisions. In this talk, Tom Stevenson explores the new shape of talent: the rare minds that can see the path worth taking in a world of infinite answers.
